description: Imports LinkedIn Marketing (Ads) ad accounts, account users, campaign groups, campaigns, creatives, conversions, and pivoted ad-analytics reports from the LinkedIn Rest.li Marketing API.

spec.apiVersionPinning: `Linkedin-Version` request header, pinned to the constant LINKEDIN_VERSION_API = "202602" and sent on every request. Additionally most streams send the Rest.li protocol header `X-Restli-Protocol-Version: 2.0.0` (Accounts sends it only when account_ids are configured; Creatives instead sends `X-RestLi-Method: FINDER`).

authTierRationale: Two credential modes are offered. The 'Access Token' mode requires only a single self-serve LinkedIn access token (documented in-code as TTL ~2 months) sent as a bearer token — that is T1_SIMPLE, and it is the easiest mode offered, so authTierOverall is T1. The 'OAuth2.0' mode is standalone T3_BYO_REFRESH: the connector's own spec requires client_id, client_secret AND refresh_token from the user, meaning the user must register their own LinkedIn developer application and complete a consent flow to obtain a refresh token. Estuary's hosted control plane can mask that: __main__.py declares a flow.OAuth2Spec with provider 'linkedin' and authUrl/accessToken templates, so in Estuary's UI the platform drives the authorization_code exchange and harvests /refresh_token on the user's behalf. That is a hosted-control-plane convenience; the standalone tier for that mode is still T3.

unionMisfits.description: For every non-analytics incremental stream (account_users, campaign_groups, campaigns, creatives, conversions) there is no distinct backfill vs incremental request. The exact same request is issued every run — a full re-listing over all parent accounts — and incrementality is achieved purely client-side by discarding records whose cursor value is below the stored state. The schema's backfill/incremental split has no correlate here; I filled only `incremental` and left `backfill` null, but the honest description is 'one pull shape, client-side filtered'.

Analytics streams DO have a genuine server-side incremental parameter, but it is not expressible as {param, format}. The window is a Rest.li structured literal `dateRange=(start:(year:Y,month:M,day:D),end:(year:Y,month:M,day:D))` built from a 30-day sliding window starting at the state cursor `end_date` (WINDOW_IN_DAYS = 30). It is neither iso8601 nor unix_seconds nor date, and it carries both bounds in one param. I set incrementalParam null rather than mis-encode it.

incrementalParam.boundsFrom: state cursor end_date -> min(window end, now-2h)

unionMisfits.description: Analytics streams fan a single logical row out across MULTIPLE HTTP requests: LinkedIn caps the analytics finder at 20 fields, so the connector chunks ~96 metric fields into groups of 18 (+dateRange+pivotValues) and issues one request per (account/campaign, date window, field chunk), then merges the responses in memory keyed by `{end_date}-{pivotValues}`. The PullSpec union assumes one request shape per record; there is no place to express request fan-out-and-merge.

The creatives stream makes an unmodelled SECOND HTTP call per record: when a creative record has no inline name, it issues GET rest/posts/{url-encoded share URN} with a hand-built Authorization: Bearer header and copies adContext.dscName into a synthetic `creative_name` field. This is a per-record enrichment lookup, not a paginated stream, and has no home in the PullSpec union.

The offset paginator terminates on a CONJUNCTION of two conditions, not one: (a) the returned `elements` array is shorter than the requested count AND (b) paging.total - paging.start <= count (treated as satisfied when either key is absent). terminateOn is a single enum value; I recorded 'short_page' because it is the necessary condition, but 'explicit_total' is equally load-bearing.

Analytics streams do not paginate — but the over-limit case is not a silent stop either: if more than 15000 elements would be returned the connector RAISES, instructing the operator to reduce time granularity. {"type":"none"} loses the fact that overflow is a hard failure rather than truncation.

Headers are not uniform across streams. `Linkedin-Version: 202602` is truly global, but the Rest.li protocol header is conditional and inconsistently spelled in the source: Accounts sends `X-RestLi-Protocol-Version` only when account_ids is configured; campaign_groups/campaigns/analytics send `X-Restli-Protocol-Version` (different capitalisation) unconditionally; conversions sends it too; creatives sends `X-RestLi-Method: FINDER` instead. defaultHeaders can only hold the global one.

For account_users and conversions the parent-derived value is not a path segment at all — it is injected as a query parameter (`accounts=` / `account=`) carrying a URN. I used pathPlaceholders because it is the only slot for parent scoping, and said so in each description, but the name is wrong for these two.

abstained.execution.defaultSchedule: Nothing in the connector or in the estuary-cdk airbyte shim sets a poll interval, cron, or sleep. shim_airbyte_cdk._run drives self.delegate.read(...) once to exhaustion per task invocation; the ResourceConfig schema (confirmed in tests/snapshots/snapshots__spec__capture.stdout.json) exposes only stream / syncMode / cursorField / namespace — no interval field. Scheduling is therefore imposed by the Flow runtime outside this connector and is not recoverable from these sources.
abstained.streams[*].schedules: Same reason as execution.defaultSchedule — there is no per-binding schedule field in ResourceConfig. Emitted as empty lists rather than invented intervals.
abstained.streams[*].writeDisposition: Not directly stated. The shim hardcodes destination_sync_mode="append" and stamps every document with meta.op="u", while the discovered collections are keyed (/id, /account, or /string_of_pivot_values+/end_date), which in Flow reduces to last-write-wins upsert. I recorded "merge" on that reasoning but flag it low confidence: no tombstones are ever emitted and no delete detection exists, so a strict reading could also call the full_refresh `accounts` binding a snapshot without tombstone.
abstained.streams[*].pull.incremental.incrementalP: Deliberately null everywhere. For the six non-analytics streams there genuinely is no server-side incremental parameter — the full parent-scoped listing is re-fetched each run and old records are dropped in Python. For the analytics streams the real mechanism is the structured Rest.li `dateRange` window, which does not fit {param, format}; see unionMisfits[1] rather than a guessed value.
abstained.streams[*].pull.backfill: Left null for every stream. The connector issues an identical request on first and subsequent runs; only the client-side state filter (non-analytics) or the starting date window (analytics) differs. Splitting one request shape across backfill and incremental would have implied two request shapes that do not exist.
abstained.configFields.end_date: analytics_streams.py reads config.get("end_date") to bound the date-slice generator, but `end_date` is NOT declared anywhere in spec.json. The spec sets additionalProperties: true so it is settable, yet it is undiscoverable from the UI. I did not list it as a configField because I cannot tell whether it is intentional dead capability or an omission from the spec.
abstained.transports[0].spec.defaultHeaders: Only `Linkedin-Version` is unconditionally global. The Rest.li protocol-version header is stream-conditional and appears under two different spellings in the source; I kept it out of defaultHeaders and described the real distribution in apiVersionPinning and unionMisfits[6].
abstained.streams[*].pull.incremental.recordsPath: Recorded as "elements" from response.json().get("elements"), which is certain. Note that the connector then applies a transform_data() flattening pass over each element before emitting, so the emitted document shape is not the raw element; that transform is not modelled by this schema.
abstained.streams[*].supportedSyncModes for analyt: Listed as [full_refresh, incremental] to match the discovered bindings, but note the analytics streams use IncrementalMixin state that advances only after a whole date slice completes across all parents — a full_refresh run would still be date-window driven from start_date. The union has no way to say that.
